s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers
salient_findings: Sudden-onset chest pain
ECG findings of ST-segment elevation and PR-segment elevation in lead aVR
Elevated high-sensitivity troponin I and brain-type natriuretic peptide
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography
Systolic apical ballooning on left ventriculography
key_facts: Female patient in her 60s
History of hypertension
No history of acute febrile illness
No family history of sudden cardiac death
Tachycardic with a pulse of 120 beats/min
Normal blood pressure
White blood cell count of 14,300/µL
Serum calcium within normal limits
High-sensitivity troponin I of 1.15 ng/mL
Brain-type natriuretic peptide of 1060.30 pg/mL
ECG findings of sinus tachycardia, PR-segment elevation in lead aVR, and ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V2 to V6
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography
Systolic apical ballooning on left ventriculography
Enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Systolic apical ballooning on left ventriculography and normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma-induced cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT and elevated cardiac biomarkers

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma crisis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to pheochromocytoma-induced cardiomyopathy, with potential for crisis due to catecholamine surge

shortlist.label: Acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated high-sensitivity troponin I and ST-segment elevation on ECG, although coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation similar to Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, with potential for stress-induced cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The presence of an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass on CT, suggestive of a pheochromocytoma, combined with the patient's presentation of chest pain, tachycardia, and elevated troponin and brain-type natriuretic peptide levels, points towards pheochromocytoma-induced cardiomyopathy as the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has systolic apical ballooning, the presence of an adrenal mass suggests a different primary cause.

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma crisis
rejected.why: Pheochromocytoma crisis typically presents with severe hypertension, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries on angiography make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: This is another term for Takotsubo cardiomyopathy and does not account for the adrenal mass found on CT.
